The ASV writes no word for the relative, rendering ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν as he ought to think, so the token is its own unrepresented unit (rule 23). The competing reading joins παρ᾽ ὅ into one aligned unit on the single English word than, which is rule 94's precondition and the shape rule 50 takes for ἕως ἄν -> till; it remains defensible. The split is taken because than answers to παρά alone and no part of it answers to the relative, and rule 50's joining is licensed there by that rule's refusal to leave ἄν empty, which no rule extends to a relative pronoun.

review_notes: παντὶ τῷ ὄντι is split three ways under rules 22, 32 and 80: to every on the quantifier with the dative preposition, man on the substantival article, that is on the participle.

ὅ is left unrepresented because the ASV renders ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν without any relative word. The competing reading joins παρ᾽ ὅ into one aligned unit on than under rules 94 and 39, as rule 50 joins ἕως ἄν -> till; it is defensible and is recorded in the unit's note, but the split is kept because than answers to παρά alone.
The correlative so of so to think as is read as a helper on the first φρονεῖν; giving it to εἰς with as remains defensible.
